about: Every user-facing feature of this repository, grouped by what it does, with the evidence that it works: the tools it uses, a guide, committed example outputs, the tests that pin them, and independent reviews of those exact outputs (data/reviews.json). The public label is 'reviewed example' when all of these exist and a passing review's recorded file hashes still match the outputs; otherwise its evidence gaps are listed. This does not establish a complete automated route, compatibility across all formats or plant acceptance. docs/FEATURES.md is generated from this file by scripts/feature_catalog.py, which CI checks.

categories.extract: Read a drawing or a structured file into a draft asset model
categories.model: Generate drawings and exports from an authored process model
categories.export: Share engineering context with other tools
categories.check: Check a drawing, a tool or this repository against something independent
categories.operate: Work with live or historical process data, and review the model
categories.screen: Find questions worth asking and the data needed to answer them

features.title: A P&ID image to a draft asset model and review bundle
features.job: Get a starting asset model out of a P&ID without retyping it
features.you_need: One P&ID as a PNG; a model subscription (or the committed example)
features.time: 88 s of commands on one new sheet (sheet 8), measured once; sheet 0's recorded run took 75 s plus 1 s; review time not measured
features.you_get: Extracted symbols, tags and links as a draft model, a review sheet, Ignition tags and PI staging. Your own-drawing sheet has no research-trained risk tiers; review priorities need your engineering judgment
features.why: Retyping drawings into asset lists takes manual effort in historian, HMI and digital twin projects. A draft turns some of that typing into checking; the time saved has not been measured.

features.title: The one-page report a client reads first
features.job: Show someone what came out of a drawing, and what still needs checking
features.you_need: A review bundle from import_site_drawing.py
features.time: Under a second
features.you_get: One page: the drawing with every item boxed, item and review status, supplied applied review records with recorded reviewer/date, next steps toward questions/context or data-connected staging, and limits. Refuses if any generated column of the review sheet doesn't match what the model gives now; the reviewer's OPS_ entries aren't checked, so decisions not yet applied with apply_review.py don't appear
features.why: The receiving engineer needs to see what was found, what is still unchecked and how to build on the model without tracing every generated file.

features.title: Adapted public DEXPI examples to a drawing bundle, with no model reading
features.job: Reproduce the configured public DEXPI examples through the drawing-intake contract
features.you_need: One of the three public DEXPI example sheets, prepared once by adapt_dexpi.py (downloads them; needs PyMuPDF). For your own DEXPI XML, use the DEXPI reader instead
features.time: Seconds once the sheets are prepared
features.you_get: The same bundle with no model reading: tags are the drawn label text, and links are the drawn connections, undirected, with each pipe tee expanded into pairwise links
features.why: A CAD export already represents symbols and connections as data. Reading supported DEXPI content directly avoids a visual model-reading step; conversion limits and omissions still need review.

features.title: Your own DEXPI XML export to a process model with its attributes kept
features.job: Turn the DEXPI XML my CAD tool exports into a model, keeping line sizes, specs and design limits
features.why: A CAD export can hold sizes, specifications and design limits. The reader preserves supported attributes with XML element citations and reports folds, placement gaps and omissions. Explicit source capture also retains the complete policy-filtered structured packet, distinguishing Native mappings from retained but uninterpreted occurrences.
features.you_need: A DEXPI P&ID XML file (tested on DEXPI 1.3, and on DEXPI 1.2 exports from SPPID, Comos, AVEVA and AutoCAD); a rendered PNG only if you also want the drawing bundle
features.time: Seconds per sheet
features.you_get: A Native process model and conversion report. Existing downstream tools can use eligible Native fields after their own validation; some converted models lack the equipment or instruments a tool requires. Optional explicit capture appends a complete policy-filtered source packet; graph/context/MCP consumers do not expose that packet.

features.title: An authored process model to draft exports and P&ID sheets
features.job: Generate drawings and exports from a sourced process model
features.you_need: A sourced process-model JSON, authored by an engineer or approved assistant from the description; detailed P&ID output also needs an authored drafting layout
features.time: Model/layout authoring and engineering review are required; their time is unmeasured
features.you_get: Logical SVGs, a review sheet and Ignition/PI staging from model JSON; a separate renderer creates detailed draft P&IDs from model plus layout. No packaged raw-description interpreter or automatic detailed layout
features.why: A source-cited draft makes an engineer's interpretation of procedures and design notes checkable. Agreement with the actual plant still needs independent records or field evidence and engineering review.

features.title: The model as an open graph of sourced claims
features.job: Load the model into an asset register, graph database or change system
features.you_need: Any model this repository produces
features.time: Seconds
features.you_get: Portable JSON of assets, three link layers and sourced claims, with full/core profiles. Selected review records remain complete and unbound; explicit supplied associations add qualified events.
features.why: Keep relationships, source qualifications and supplied review history together for another engineer to inspect or an explicitly implemented receiving adapter to preserve.

features.title: Ignition tags and PI AF staging from a model
features.job: Get the model into Ignition and PI
features.you_need: A reviewed model
features.time: Seconds to generate; import is a manual step in a lab gateway
features.you_get: Ignition tag import with UDTs, PI Builder staging sheets; values are placeholders until mapped
features.why: Generating the Ignition tag structure and PI asset staging from one model keeps them consistent with each other and avoids repeated manual entry. Native import still needs a lab check.

features.title: A supplied loop list checked against a drawing key or model
features.job: Compare a supplied loop list with a drawing key or model
features.you_need: A reviewed simple-loop list (controller, measurement, output) and a corresponding drawing key or extracted model
features.time: Seconds
features.you_get: Key: drawn, partly drawn or not drawn; extracted model: tag presence only. Vendor intake example preserves multi-connection functions without inventing loops.
features.why: Controls records and drawings can disagree. Comparing supplied records exposes differences to investigate; current installed behavior still needs site evidence.

features.title: Any digitization tool scored beside perfect, wrong and empty answers
features.job: Find out whether a digitization tool or vendor is actually accurate on our drawings
features.you_need: Your sheets and corresponding hand-labelled GraphML keys in the documented format, plus saved tool answers; the public tutorial supplies a worked comparison
features.time: Seconds once labelled; labelling takes hours
features.you_get: A score beside perfect, wrong and empty answers, per sheet, refusing to report if the scorer can be fooled
features.why: Vendors quote accuracy on their own test drawings. Scoring them on yours, with a deliberately wrong answer scored beside them, shows whether the number means anything.

features.title: A public drawing added to the benchmark with an independently verified key
features.job: Add a public P&ID and its answer key so every drawing reader is measured on more sheets
features.you_need: A public drawing whose license you have confirmed, a starting extraction or a blank key, and a second person to review a sample
features.time: Minutes for the tool; correcting a key takes hours
features.you_get: A case folder with source, license and exposure recorded, a review receipt bound to the key's hash, passing known-answer controls and a validation entry in a benchmark suite
features.why: A reader is only as well measured as the drawings it is tested on. Each checked public drawing makes every comparison harder to fool; the review samples what the author left as the model drafted it, where anchoring hides.

features.title: Plug a different drawing reader into the same pipeline, and compare readers on one leaderboard
features.job: Bring a better reader (trained model, vendor API, fine-tuned model) and keep the review queue, sources and exports around it
features.you_need: Your reader's per-sheet output and a small adapter to the documented prediction format; answer keys to score it
features.time: Seconds to convert and import one sheet; scoring as for the vendor-evaluation kit
features.you_get: An importable prediction file, the same review bundle and exports as the current reader, and a registered result shown beside the controls, labelled development, validation or held-out. The worked example re-expresses an existing reading; no other reader has been run yet
features.why: The current reader drafts and is the most replaceable part. A reader that plugs into the same slot can be measured on the same keys and inherit everything around it.

features.title: Checks a stranger (or their agent) can run on this repository
features.job: Decide whether to trust this repository at all
features.you_need: Python alone for claim and freshness checks; full tests also need Git, pinned packages and required public caches; optional-source omissions are reported separately
features.time: Under a minute for the claim check
features.you_get: Headline claims checked against results files, stage freshness, and selected tests with skipped cases and coverage limits visible
features.why: Before trusting any tool with your plant's data, you should be able to check its claims yourself in minutes.

features.title: Normal bands and an OPC UA replay from historian CSV exports
features.job: Learn normal operating bands from history, or test screens against recorded data
features.you_need: Historian exports as CSV: one of normal running, optionally one of an upset. Standard library only; the replay server also needs asyncua
features.time: Seconds
features.you_get: Bands per tag with false-alarm rates, the first tag to leave its band in an upset, and an OPC UA server replaying the CSV
features.why: History can highlight unusual changes, and replaying recorded data lets you test new screens without touching the live system. Detection before an operational alarm is not guaranteed.

features.title: Reviewer decisions back into the model, and instruments mapped to supplied addresses
features.job: Apply review decisions and assign supplied OPC or PI addresses
features.you_need: A filled review sheet; the plant's I/O list
features.time: Seconds per apply; the review itself is people's time
features.you_get: An updated draft model and dated review record; source-referenced OPC/PI assignments and an optional graph handoff with complete review evidence and supplied association qualifications
features.why: Source-referenced corrections and addresses make a draft easier to check and hand off. Source records and address assignments do not establish plant truth, connectivity or signal identity.

features.title: Selected workflows checked across registered public inputs
features.job: Find out whether a tool will work on drawings or data like mine, not just the ones it was built on
features.why: A workflow that only saw one set of drawings can fail on the next. Eight selected workflows run across registered applicable inputs, showing where they hold and break, red cells included; other features have their own tests and examples.
features.you_need: Nothing to read the page; the public datasets (fetched by script) to re-run it
features.time: Reading: minutes. Re-running everything: about 25 minutes of cell time, plus downloading the public data once
features.you_get: A pass/fail grid with reasons and declared code, input/key, registry and runner bindings from actual runs. Missing optional caches are explicitly unverified; strict --require-inputs requires them. Workflow criteria and independent-source limits remain separate from completion percentages

features.title: Energy, heat-grade and controls questions worth asking of a drawing, and the data to answer them
features.job: Find energy, heat-grade and control questions worth asking about my unit, and what data answers each
features.why: Many energy and controls questions can be spotted on a P&ID before anyone collects data: a throttled pump, high-pressure steam let down for a low-temperature job, heat dumped to cooling water, a loop with no controller. A solo engineer rarely has time to look. This lists the questions with the evidence by tag and exactly what to collect, and where, to settle each one, without inventing a savings number.
features.you_need: A process model or extracted drawing set; optionally the plant's loop list and equipment schedules
features.time: Seconds
features.you_get: Per question and asset: the evidence by tag, what to collect and where (down to a blank field on a named schedule), how the data decides it, and what public sources say is typical. A screen, not an audit

features.title: First-draft annual energy, cost and CO2e from a measured change, with its assumptions and the data to firm it up
features.job: Turn a change I measured into an annual energy, cost and greenhouse-gas figure
features.why: A measured change becomes a first-draft cost and emissions figure, good enough to decide whether to collect better data, with every constant's source shown and every assumption listed. If you don't have a constant, it tells you exactly which bill, contract or public table has it.
features.you_need: What you measured (kW before and after, steam lb/h, fuel saved, hours) and your tariff, gas price, emission factors and boiler efficiency, or labelled public typical values
features.time: Minutes
features.you_get: A first-draft estimate, marked as one: annual kWh or MMBtu, cost and CO2e with the formula and source of every constant, the assumptions it rests on, and the data to collect (and where) to replace each one; or, per question, what to measure and where each constant comes from

features.title: Every output as plain statements, checked against its source
features.job: Measure how often the model's statements match their sources, and let an operator check a unit in plain English
features.why: "Does this look right?" has no answer you can track. A sampled review of plain sentences against their sources gives an error rate for each kind of statement, and keeps 'matches the drawing' apart from 'true in the plant', which only someone who knows the unit can say.
features.you_need: A graph export (twin-graph-1), plus the sheet image or report PDF its sources cite
features.time: Seconds to render; review time per statement not yet measured
features.you_get: A stratified sample of plain sentences, each beside its drawing crop or report page, with two separate verdict columns; an error rate with a 95% interval; and the verdicts written back into the graph as dated events

features.title: Prepare a first engineering evidence and decision packet
features.job: Build a first evidence and decision packet for company handoff
features.why: A first investigation should leave its question, source revisions, competing evidence and reasons together. Another person can review that packet; a shared company system takes over ongoing ownership and coordination.
features.you_need: A draft model or graph, a question list, local source documents and their revision/locator manifest; an engineer to assign and review answers
features.time: Local packet preparation; engineering review time has not been measured
features.you_get: A local context report, evidence-bound dated decisions and ownership history, unanswered/disputed/stale queues, and versioned JSON plus enriched graph/questions for handoff. The receiving company system supplies shared access and ongoing governance

features.title: Read a selected graph snapshot through bounded internal MCP tools
features.job: Let an approved local assistant retrieve assets, relations and questions from one cleared packet
features.why: A sourced engineering packet becomes reusable through a standard assistant interface while the company keeps authority over its records and decisions.
features.you_need: An approved IT developer environment, optional pinned MCP SDK, and a selected twin-graph-1 JSON snapshot; optional explicitly selected context-register-1 sidecar; shared authentication and Copilot reachability require separate work
features.time: Local developer setup; company deployment and engineering review time unmeasured
features.you_get: Nine read-only snapshot tools and a summary resource, with source claims, statuses, fingerprints, stream identities and bounded paging. An explicitly selected, hash-bound context sidecar adds full retained answer/decision/source readback. Local SDK/stdio/loopback tests; no source fetching, process-data connector or shared company deployment

features.title: A description packet through approved-assistant authoring to a checked draft bundle
features.job: Connect a written description to a locally checkable model, drawing, questions and graph
features.why: Engineers need a usable authoring contract and feedback loop between their approved assistant and the separate generation tools. One packet makes the interpretation, unknowns and resulting outputs inspectable before company handoff.
features.you_need: Cleared UTF-8 description, an engineer or approved assistant to author native model/layout JSON, and approved Python/drawing dependencies for local checks and generation
features.time: Authored development fixtures only; assistant quality and engineering review time unmeasured
features.you_get: Numbered source/prompt/contract, exact quotation and directed consistency feedback, then draft P&ID PNG/SVG, questions, graph and platform staging with payload hashes. Full supplied-record interpretation and source-line review sheets start unreviewed. No automatic interpretation/layout, tested Copilot tenant or plant approval

features.title: Contribute corpus cases and compare saved model/method runs by task
features.job: Improve a toolkit task with source-backed corpus cases, reproducible model results and baseline regression evidence
features.why: New examples should expose failures and support tested generalizations. Matched task/source/key/scorer cohorts make comparisons inspectable without conflating model versions, methods, source families or incomplete coverage.
features.you_need: Cleared source and reviewed key with provenance, a supported versioned task, saved answers for declared attempts, model/interface/configuration and pinned recipe metadata; no model account needed to re-score
features.time: Offline rescoring; model execution and human source/key review are separate contributions
features.you_get: Per-case results for four task families: drawing structure, selected description facts, fixed claim labels and tag reading (separate geometry/list modes). An optional reviewed Native model-value profile binds declared values/groups before the same label scorer. Coverage, reviewer accuracy and contradicted statements are reported separately. Exposed saved answers and synthetic development controls do not establish held-out or general source/model accuracy. Reason quality, source authority and current plant truth remain unscored; other tasks need reviewed evaluators.

features.title: Carry a converted model and its captured source evidence to review
features.job: Prepare and inspect a local model/evidence packet for an approved company handoff
features.why: Another reviewer or receiving system needs the converted model and the captured evidence it leaves uninterpreted. An explicit three-file packet preserves both with checked bindings and a qualified brief, while company systems retain ongoing ownership, access and decisions.
features.you_need: An already source-bearing model from explicit DEXPI capture, an approved local root, and supplied scope/role labels; originals remain separate
features.time: Local file processing; human review and transfer effort have not been measured
features.you_get: A Native model projection, complete policy-filtered captured evidence, hash-bound manifest and bounded inspection brief. No automatic source capture, company approval, access control, atomic publication or source-aware MCP consumer.

features.title: Read and retain source-qualified engineering contributions
features.job: Give an engineer or intern a sourced starting map and one reviewable document-only assignment
features.why: People need prior reasoning, source locations and a receiving reviewer before proposing a change. A selected landing map, glossary, role references and starter workflow keep the first contribution connected while company systems retain authority.
features.you_need: A cleared engineering-onboarding-1 packet, a named reviewer and existing company handoff route; fictional A/B/C examples are supplied. Python standard library for direct reads; an approved client and optional pinned SDK for MCP. For local capture: an unbound packet, an authored knowledge-capture-1 change request and explicitly selected complete UTF-8 source files.
features.time: Setup, source preparation, mentoring effort and onboarding benefit have not been measured
features.you_get: Three read-only operations for a landing map, metadata lookup and complete records, including captured text, explicit unknown originals, attributed memory and fully readable stale workflows. Selected packet/selection hashes and explicit restart; no source fetching, full-text search, workflow execution, shared SSO/ACLs or company acceptance. A separate local writer appends authored claims/sources to a new packet, retaining exact prior/change files, a readable handoff and source/dependency diagnostics. No semantic answer verification or company approval.

features.title: Recorded phase calculations linked to selected twin assets
features.job: Calculate phase feed/energy from recorded data with coverage visible
features.why: Explicit recipe windows and units make recorded feed/energy calculations inspectable beside the twin; a bad sample cannot silently become a complete phase total.
features.you_need: A bounded elapsed-time CSV, supplied phase/unit plan and optional explicitly selected twin-graph-1; Python 3.10+, standard library only.
features.time: Not measured on plant-scale data.
features.you_get: JSON/Markdown phase means, extrema, rate integrals and coverage, explicit V2 interpolation/quality policies, original source and method hashes, optional exact graph-ID binding; fictional controls and one measured laboratory-series calculation. No prediction, installed signal acceptance or live connector. Explicit selected-file/code basis checks reproduce the complete saved result when pins match; no automatic source monitoring or context refresh. Explicit local batch/event/executed-recipe/lab/outcome joins, declared availability/quality gaps, bounded upstream calculation freshness, full audit/raw originals and descriptive differences. No general/live ingestion, causal or yield inference, historical-access proof or accepted investigation outcome.

features.title: One map of P&IDs, equipment and instrument records, datasheets and documents, with owner-routed conflicts
features.job: Connect a site's plant records and documents across plants
features.you_need: P&ID sheets read by the drawing reader (converted with one_map.py sheet-from-prediction) or authored sheet reads, a sheet index, whatever equipment and instrument records exist (maintenance equipment export, instrument index, loop list), optional datasheets and a document manifest (PDF, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, HTML or text documents); a site file naming plants, units, shared systems, record owners and which record is authoritative for which kind of fact
features.time: Seconds
features.you_get: A twin-graph-2 graph (site/plant/unit hierarchy, P&ID locations by sheet zone, documents with covers/based_on and mentions found in PDF/Office/HTML/text with a locator, exact or format-insensitive), conflict records routed to the owner of the non-authoritative record, low-priority P&ID value notes, located-loop outcomes, a risk-sorted review queue split by owner/plant/unit, and a draft maintenance equipment export, instrument index and loop list where none exists; item classes, links that do not fit what they connect, completeness rules (expected but missing, certified and rolled out per unit or owner), plant glossary terms in document matching (OCR text never links), read-only answers with sources or 'can't answer from this map', and an optional JSON-LD view. Prototype on fictional records and one public development P&ID sheet; no plant acceptance
features.why: Departments keep their own records and documents; disagreements between them stay invisible until someone compares by hand. One graph keeps each record's source and owner, takes each value from the record that owns it, and sends each disagreement to the person who owns the record.

features.title: Read the text inside PDF, Word, Excel, PowerPoint and HTML documents, with a locator for every piece
features.job: Read procedures, HACCP plans, PHAs, CAPAs, work orders and purchase orders so the tags they mention can be found
features.you_need: The documents (.pdf, .docx/.docm, .xlsx/.xlsm, .pptx/.pptm, .html, .txt, .md, .csv); for PDF text, the optional pypdf package or a pdftotext program. Optional, only when asked for: Tesseract (and Poppler pdftoppm) for OCR of scanned pages and images, LibreOffice for legacy .doc/.xls/.ppt/.rtf
features.time: Seconds per document
features.you_get: One text file per document with a locator before each piece (page 3, paragraph 12, table 2 row 4, sheet 'PM plan' cell B7, slide 4, line 9) and a manifest with each file's SHA-256, status and warnings. Embedded Office/PDF files are read with their place (embedded 'spec.pdf' (in table 3) page 2). Scanned pages are reported as needing OCR and legacy .doc/.xls with a conversion step, unless the optional --ocr auto or --convert-legacy add-ons and their programs are used; --pdf-layout and --excel-display are further opt-ins. Prototype on fictional and public files; OCR and conversion tested with stand-in programs and, where installed, the real Tesseract, Poppler and LibreOffice (OCR accuracy measured on rendered and scanned public pages); no plant acceptance
features.why: Procedures, PHAs, CAPAs and work orders name the same equipment as the P&ID and the instrument index, but they live in Office files and PDFs that a text search cannot see. A locator on every piece lets a reviewer open the document at the place a tag was found.

features.title: Source-retaining DXF attribute handoff
features.job: Retain a drawing and inspect proposed equipment-attribute edits before a controlled handoff
features.you_need: A DXF in the declared block-attribute profile, stable ICT_ID/TAG values, ezdxf and an explicit hash-bound edit plan
features.time: No human-effort measurement; authored and public-adapted software cases, native API and display checks are not a timed plant trial
features.you_get: Exact original and proposed value-span DXFs, optional source-bound local form/agent JSON exchange, frozen decoded comparison plus independent raw reconstruction, retained native full-save differences and mapped draft CAD-reference revisions; no inferred pipe relationships
features.why: Editable drawings need stable identities and unfamiliar data retained. Source-preserving metadata exchange is separate from native full-save failures. One exposed Linux valve has actual native UI edit/save/reopen evidence; complete layout/font acceptance, fresh native validation, intelligent-CAD databases and company acceptance remain open.

features.title: Public nameplate candidates with retained OCR failures
features.job: Prepare source-linked field candidates from photos without inventing an installed equipment match
features.you_need: Public originals for the example; permitted source/capture grouping, Tesseract for optional replay, and an independent field/identity reviewer for site use
features.time: Human capture/review effort and field accuracy unmeasured
features.you_get: Two attributed public photographs, visual field candidates awaiting independent review, six retained OCR attempts including failures, explicit unknown identity
features.why: OCR can return plausible text while missing numeric equipment data. Original evidence, units, unreadable values and unconfirmed identity must survive record preparation.

features.title: Explicitly mapped maintenance exports to a sourced offline manager packet
features.job: Reconcile selected equipment records against recorded installed values on closed work orders, retaining a review packet across revisions
features.you_need: Two permitted CSVs, explicit reviewed profile with identities/field meanings/source revisions/coverage/owners, Python 3.10+ standard library
features.time: Human preparation/review/benefit unmeasured; exposed fictional software replay only
features.you_get: Exact originals, normalized records and row origins, one-map graph/queue, readable draft report, proposed actions, inventory and explicit prior-packet comparison
features.why: Ordinary exports need a repeatable self-service path that preserves scope and source history without confusing disappeared disagreements with accepted corrections.
